order.title: Decision order
order.description: By default every request walks these four checks in this order, and the first one to decide, decides. A whitelist match ends the walk immediately: the request is allowed and the three checks after it never run. The order itself is configurable per service, through PLUGINS_ORDER_ACCESS and PLUGINS_ORDER_PREREAD.

kinds.title: What is matched
kinds.description: One section per kind of match. In each, the entries you type and the lists BunkerWeb downloads are checked together; a client matching either one matches the section.

unplaced.title: Other settings
unplaced.description: Declared by the plugin but not yet given a place on this page. They still save normally.

enforcement.description: The whitelist runs first and overrides everything else: a match is allowed straight through, so blacklist, greylist and country never see the request. Bans are the one exception, and only by IP — a client matched here by reverse DNS, ASN, user agent or URI is still blocked while it is banned. Keep this list to the clients that must never be locked out.
The blacklist runs after the whitelist, so a client that is whitelisted is never blocked here. On each row, the exception lists override that row's own entries and downloaded lists.

community.title: Community lists
community.description: Curated lists maintained outside BunkerWeb and refreshed for you. They feed the same matching as the entries below.

enforcement.description: The greylist is deny-by-default: while it is on, anything that matches none of the entries below is denied, on HTTP and on stream traffic alike. Add the entries first, then turn it on — a save that enables it with every list empty is refused.

greylist.locked_out: Greylisting is on and no entry is configured, so every request to this service is denied. Add at least one entry below, or turn greylisting off.

country.title: Country rule
country.description: One rule, not two lists. Allowing a set of countries denies every other country and makes a stored block list dead configuration — BunkerWeb checks the allow list first and never reaches the block list.

conflict.description: Both country lists are stored, and only the allow list is enforced: the block list below is never consulted while an allow list is set.

exceptions.title: Exceptions
exceptions.description: Requests whose URI matches one of these patterns skip the country rule entirely.

rules.title: Composite rules
rules.description: A rule matches only when every one of its terms matches. Rules are checked alongside the lists above and a client matching any one of them matches this stage. Values may be a resource group, written @name.
rules.negate_help: Invert this term: the rule matches when the term does NOT match.

engine.title: Engine
engine.description: Whether ModSecurity is loaded at all, and what it does with a rule match.

crs.title: OWASP Core Rule Set
crs.description: The shared rule set BunkerWeb loads on top of ModSecurity. Version 4 is the current one; version 3 is kept for services that still depend on its rule ids.

crs_plugins.title: Core Rule Set plugins
crs_plugins.description: Rule packs published for the Core Rule Set, downloaded and installed at startup. Give a plugin name, a name/tag, or a URL.

global_crs.title: Global CRS mode
global_crs.description: Loads the Core Rule Set once for the whole instance instead of once per service. Faster to load with many services, but service-scoped modsec-crs configs are refused while it is on: create a global one and scope it with a Host rule instead.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.description: What ModSecurity writes to its own audit log, and how much of each transaction it keeps. Parts A and Z are always included.

limits.title: Request body limits
limits.description: How much of a request body ModSecurity inspects, and what happens to a body that exceeds the limit. NGINX enforces MAX_CLIENT_SIZE first, so a limit above it has no effect.

tuning.title: Rule tuning
tuning.description: Clearing a false positive is a custom config, not a setting. These are the four places a rule exclusion can go, in the order they are loaded.

notice.off: ModSecurity is off. Nothing below is applied, but every value is kept and comes back when you turn it on again.
notice.engine_off: ModSecurity is enabled but SecRuleEngine is Off, so no request is inspected. These two settings both mean "on" and they currently disagree.
notice.engine_detect: SecRuleEngine is DetectionOnly: matches are logged and nothing is blocked.
notice.crs_v3_no_plugins: Core Rule Set 3 cannot load plugins. The plugin switch and plugin list are kept and will apply again on version 4, but they do nothing right now.

csp.title: Content Security Policy
csp.description: The policy sent as Content-Security-Policy. A wrong directive breaks the site's own scripts with nothing to see server-side, so report-only first is the safe order.

permissions.title: Permissions Policy
permissions.description: Which browser features this site may use, as a comma-separated list of feature=(allowlist) clauses. An entry left at () disables that API for everyone, including your own pages.

transport.title: HTTPS enforcement
transport.description: The Strict-Transport-Security header. Only sent over HTTPS.

browser.title: Browser protections
browser.description: Small fixed-value headers. An empty value removes the header instead of sending it.

upstream.title: Upstream and removed headers
upstream.description: Which of the upstream's own response headers survive, and which are stripped before the response leaves.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.description: Flags added to every Set-Cookie the upstream returns. Per-cookie flag rules are in the repeatable settings below.

notice.keep_all: The keep list is *, so every header the upstream sends wins over the values configured here.
